newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal-Some offers slip as demand slows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal-Some offers slip as demand slows.

text.p: Some soymeal basis offers in U.S. cash markets weakened slightly Friday in response to an expected drop-off in demand, U.S. cash dealers said.
"I think we're entering into a period where exports and domestic business both will slow down," said one Kansas City-based broker.
Soymeal movement was said to be very slow in most markets Friday, but one Illinois dealer reported end-user pricing.
The weekly soybean crush from the National Oilseed Processor's Association of 26.2 million bushels fell within trade expectations for 25.5 to 26.5 million bushels.
Last week's lower-than-expected crush of 25.9 million bushels was said to be caused in part by unexpected downtimes at some southeastern crushing facilities, dealers said.
"We saw some unexpected downtime last week, but those plants are probably back on line by now," said one river dealer.
